title: Data Glitches Discovery using Influence-based Model Explanations

problem.claim: Detect mislabeled and anomalous samples in machine-learning training sets.

gap.claim: Model-agnostic glitch detectors may detect samples inconsistent with the predictive model's decision boundary because they replicate fitting the data distribution.

contributions.claim: A methodology uses influence functions to estimate how removing a sample affects model or sample loss.
Three influence-based signals detect, characterize, and repair data glitches in training sets.
The influence-based signals form an explainable-by-design data-glitch detection framework tied to the actual predictive model.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce three novel signals for detecting, characterizing, and repairing data glitches.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Computational experiments on tabular and image data report that the proposed signals outperform existing influence-based signals by up to a factor of 6 in some cases and generalize across datasets and machine-learning models.
The proposed signals often outperform specialized glitch detectors and provide accurate label repairs for mislabeled samples.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets detection of mislabeled and anomalous training samples.
Detecting and repairing glitches is presented as a way to understand data quality and potentially improve model reliability and performance.
The methodology uses sample influence on model or sample loss to construct three detection, characterization, and repair signals.
Influence-based signals are designed to provide explanations aligned with the predictive model, unlike model-agnostic detectors that may be inconsistent with its decision boundary.
Experiments on tabular and image data report comparative performance, cross-dataset and cross-model generalization, and accurate label repairs.

source_observation.claim: Data-quality signals based on sample influence are aligned with the predictive model and are intended to be intuitively explainable.

interpretation.claim: Data debugging may be more actionable when diagnostic scores reflect the behavior of the deployed model rather than only the marginal data distribution.

application.claim: Use model-aware influence signals to prioritize suspicious samples for investigation or label repair.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which datasets, models, or conditions determine when the reported advantages hold.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three signals or their algorithms.
The abstract does not report dataset names, model architectures, sample sizes, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not quantify label-repair accuracy or the conditions behind the reported factor-of-6 improvement.
